headline: PHP flaws prompt millions of hacking attempts amid rush to patch vulnerabilities

members.title: PHP flaws prompt millions of hacking attempts amid rush to patch vulnerabilities
members.lead: Global firms and governments rushed on Thursday to patch critical flaws in the PHP programming language that underpins much of the internet, as a cloud firm reported millions of hacking attempts after vulnerabilities were disclosed. The push came after governments in Europe and elsewhere took websites offline as a precaution on Wednesday while website operators scrambled to secure systems running the software. The emergency shutdowns of banking, airline, rail, tax and government services from Tokyo to Helsinki mark one of the most dramatic tests of the decades-old programming tools that keep the web running, exposing how deeply governments and companies depend on code that few people understand. . "I've not seen anything like this in a long, long time," Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella said at an event in Germany on Thursday, saying the incident showed the importance of building software that can be maintained securely as systems grow more complex. "It was a long day and a long night, I know, for all the IT and security folks." . The developers of PHP - a key computing language like HTML and Python - released fixes on Wednesday for vulnerabilities that had lurked in the software for years until they were uncovered using AI, urging users to "update immediately". Madeline Lawrence, co-founder of Belgian cybersecurity firm Aikido Security, said that details of the flaws had become public before fixes were ready, with attacks reported since. "Companies are racing to update against attackers who can use AI to exploit them. That's the whole race," she said. As companies and governments deployed patches and suspended websites as a precaution, hacking attempts surged into the millions, according to cloud services firm Cloudflare. . "In the 10 hours before it was publicly announced, across the network we saw thousands of attempts to exploit it," Cloudflare CEO Matthew Prince said in a post on X late on Wednesday. members.title: Bangladesh Bank website shut down to prevent cyberattacks
members.lead: The official website of Bangladesh Bank has been kept offline due to concerns over a possible cyber-attack. However, internet banking and mobile banking transactions are functioning normally, so customers are not facing any issues with their transactions. Regarding this, Bangladesh Bank spokesperson Arif Hossain Khan told Prothom Alo on Thursday night that the website is being checked for any faults. This decision was made due to concerns about worldwide attacks. There are no problems for customers in their transactions as a result. Currently, the internet and software are extremely important for delivering government services, banking, e-commerce, media, and various online platforms. . A significant portion of these websites relies on the PHP programming language. Recently, after two critical security flaws were identified in PHP, there has been global concern about cyber security. According to BBC and Reuters reports, after two critical security flaws were found in PHP, a widely used programming language for developing and managing websites, various governments have taken emergency actions. Following the news of the flaws, governments and commercial enterprises worldwide have shut down their websites since Wednesday night. Despite this, there have been millions of hacking attempts reported. Using artificial intelligence (AI), a researcher has discovered two highly dangerous flaws in a programming language called PHP. . This programming language has been used in nearly 70 per cent of websites around the world. BBC's cyber affairs correspondent, Joe Tidy, said that this is an unprecedented situation where IT teams have been scrambling to protect their organisations from a highly serious cyber attack risk, resulting in one website after another going offline. For example, the Edinburgh Council website, the ''Doctor Who'' section of the BBC website, and websites of various companies in Japan, Belgium, and the Netherlands have been taken offline. .
